content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions, primarily involving calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, famotidine, and other agents. 1. Calcium carbonate reduces the absorption and effectiveness of rifampin when co-administered. Rifampin should be taken at least 1 hour before antacids to avoid this interaction. 2. Famotidine decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, which reduces rilpivirine's solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 3. Calcium carbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 4. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by at least 1 hour. 6. Famotidine decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 8. Multivalent cation-containing products impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. 9. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of risedronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by 30 minutes. 10. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. 11. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 12. Famotidine increases the levels of serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to extended-release formulations. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 13. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of sodium phosphates (IV) by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Calcium also decreases serum phosphate concentrations by binding dietary phosphate. 14. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the effects of sodium phosphates (IV) by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Magnesium decreases serum phosphate concentrations by binding dietary phosphate. 15. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of calcium carbonate. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. 16. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Velpatasvir is practically insoluble at pH > 5. 18. Famotidine decreases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. H2 receptor antagonists may be administered simultaneously or 12 hours apart at doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. 19. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of sotalol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. 20. Vadadustat increases the levels of famotidine by affecting OAT3 substrates. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Monitor for adverse effects of OAT3 substrates and adjust doses accordingly. 21. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, which may reduce its efficacy. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Sparsentan should be administered 2 hours before or after antacids. 22. Calcium carbonate increases the toxicity of squill by an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of strontium ranelate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. 24. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by 30 minutes. 25. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of timolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. 26. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of trandolapril by an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of ursodiol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of vadadustat by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Vadadustat should be administered at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after non-iron-containing phosphate binders. 29. Famotidine increases the levels of varenicline by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of verapamil by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Vitamin D increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing serum magnesium concentrations, particularly in patients with renal impairment. Combined use of vitamin D and magnesium-containing products should be avoided in patients with chronic renal failure. 32. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Administration should be separated by 30 minutes. 33. Famotidine increases the levels of alendronate by an unspecified mechanism. Monitor for increased alendronate side effects. 34. Amikacin decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. 35. Amikacin decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Amiloride decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing renal clearance. Amiloride increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by decreasing renal clearance. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 37. Famotidine decreases the levels of aripiprazole by an unspecified mechanism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 39. Calcium carbonate increases salicylate levels at moderate doses but decreases them at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. This interaction is mediated by passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. 40. Bendroflumethiazide increases the levels of calcium carbonate by decreasing renal clearance. Bendroflumethiazide decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 41. Blessed thistle decreases the effects of famotidine and calcium carbonate by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 42. Bumetanide decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Cyclopenthiazide decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. Cyclopenthiazide increases the levels of calcium carbonate by decreasing renal clearance. The significance of these interactions is unknown. There is a risk of alkalosis and hypercalcemia. 47. Deflazacort decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing elimination. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Dextrose decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Devil's claw decreases the effects of famotidine and calcium carbonate by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 50. Dexamethasone decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing elimination. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Doxercalciferol increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents.
